text:
anne (support): Customer escalated: streaming session abruptly closes after ~35-45s idle. Last JSON chunk truncated, client reconnect gets 502. ticket #4328.
raj (eng-runtime): Can you share request id and any edge logs? Fronted by ALB/NLB/Cloudflare?
anne (support): req=rid_9b2c, customer uses Cloudflare -> NLB TCP -> our ingress. Edge log shows 200 then connection reset. They say it only triggers when stream has no activity for ~30-40s.
tony (customer): Repro steps I ran locally: 
1) curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.test/v1/streams/chat -d '{"prompt":"idle test"}'
2) wait 35-45s without sending any data
3) stream stops mid-object, last JSON fragment truncated, then reconnect returns 502.
Client error: \"read: connection reset by peer\"

anne (support): Backend gateway log for rid_9b2c: 
\"upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: stream-gw, request: \"GET /v1/streams/chat HTTP/1.1\", upstream: \"http://10.0.14.8:8080/\", host: \"api.redwood.test\"\"

ops-bot: Config summary: NLB health-check interval=10s, ALB idle_timeout=60s, Cloudflare origin keepalive=90s, nginx proxy_read_timeout=60s, gzip enabled at edge.

raj (eng-runtime): Pattern looks like an idle half-close or proxy reset during TCP reuse. Two likely causes: (1) Cloudflare + HTTP/2 stream reset when underlying TCP is recycled by NLB/OS; (2) proxy buffering/gzip coalescing delays flush so the final bytes get dropped on half-close.

raj (eng-runtime): Quick tests to isolate: 
- Bypass Cloudflare (direct DNS/origin) to see if problem persists.
- Force HTTP/1.1 to origin to rule out h2 stream reset: add -H \"Upgrade: \" and curl flag --http1.1.
- Try a keepalive padding test: send tiny server-side heartbeats ("\n") every 15s from gateway layer (not model tokens).

raj (eng-runtime): Example curl to force HTTP/1.1 and explicit keepalive:

curl -v -N --http1.1 -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" https://api.redwood.test/v1/streams/chat -d '{"prompt":"idle pad test"}'

raj (eng-runtime): If bypass eliminates the issue, CF is likely the culprit (h2->tcp reuse race). If bypass doesn't help, look at NLB target replacement/health-checks closing sockets mid-stream.

anne (support): Customer asked whether heartbeats will affect billing.
raj (eng-runtime): Heartbeats implemented at HTTP/gateway layer (single whitespace byte "\n") before the request reaches model tokenization will not be billed. If you must emit model tokens for heartbeats, that would be billable. We'll aim to implement at proxy/gateway.

raj (eng-runtime): We need PCAPs to determine who sent RST/FIN. Please collect tcpdump from both edge and pod around the disconnect window. Commands:

# on backend pod
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/stream-rid_9b2c-backend.pcap host 10.2.3.4 and port 8080

# on edge (ingress host)
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/stream-rid_9b2c-edge.pcap host <customer-ip> and port 443

# on Cloudflare side (if customer can capture)
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/cf-rid_9b2c.pcap host <edge-ip> and port 443

anne (support): I'll ask customer for PCAPs and request edge team grab the ingress capture. Assigned to eng-runtime for RCA when captures arrive. @raj can you own?

raj (eng-runtime): I'll take it. Potential short-term mitigations: 
- Add server-side heartbeat bytes every 10-15s at gateway to avoid proxies treating stream as idle.
- Set nginx directives for streaming endpoints: 
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
  gzip off;
  proxy_send_timeout 180;
  proxy_read_timeout 180;
- If ALB involved, align ALB/NLB/OS/TCP timeouts: increase ALB idle_timeout > 120s and NLB target deregistration delay so open sockets aren't closed during target rotation.

tony (customer): I can run direct-origin tests and upload a pcap. One question: is there any known Cloudflare setting that coalesces chunked frames and causes truncation?

raj (eng-runtime): Cloudflare has an optimization layer that may buffer small responses or re-chunk over HTTP/2, and compression at edge can coalesce chunks. Disabling HTTP/2 to origin or turning off response compression for streaming routes usually prevents coalescing. Also some CF features like 'Origin TCP Pooling' can reuse connections aggressively and expose half-close races.

support-bot: Escalation created -> eng-runtime. SLA: respond within 24h.

anne (support): Plan of action: 1) get PCAPs (customer + ingress) 2) customer to attempt direct origin and HTTP/1.1 test 3) apply temporary heartbeat at gateway and nginx proxy_buffering off for streaming routes 4) collect traces and tcpdump to pinpoint RST origin 5) if NLB probe race confirmed, tune NLB/ALB timeouts and health check behavior. I'll update ticket in 3 hours or when PCAPs arrive.

tony (customer): Thanks, will try bypass and upload pcap within the hour.

raj (eng-runtime): If PCAP shows RST from NLB or host OS, fix will be adjusting health-check and connection drain settings. If RST comes from Cloudflare edge, next step is to involve CF support and recommend origin keepalive alignment or disable h2 to origin. Either way, heartbeat + proxy_buffering off is a safe immediate mitigation.

anne (support): Closing loop on Slack: triage in progress, eng-runtime owns investigation. Next update when we have captures.
